# Repository template

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Overview

This repository is a technology-neutral starting point for projects coordinated by human contributors and AI coding agents. It supplies source-controlled product intent, architectural decisions, agent operating rules, reusable roles and procedures, and a minimal GitHub delivery pipeline. **It is a template, not an implemented application.**

The public README is an overview of the repository and onboarding process, **not** the product requirements document. Requirements are authored in `.agents/requests/` and compiled into `.agents/PRD.md`; architecture is authored in `.agents/decisions/` and compiled into `.agents/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

### Getting started

1. Replace the starter goal in `.agents/GOAL.md` with a specific outcome and measurable acceptance criteria.
2. Add an approved request to `.agents/requests/` and accepted architectural choices to `.agents/decisions/`.
3. Adjust `.agents/rules/` for project-specific conventions, then select the relevant role and skill instructions.
4. Regenerate committed docs: `python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --write`.
5. Verify: `python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --check`, then the project's own build/test commands when an application exists.

_Source: [0001-overview.md](notes/0001-overview.md)_


## Repository layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.agents/GOAL.md` | Human-authored purpose and success criteria |
| `.agents/PRD.md` | Generated approved product requirements |
| `.agents/ARCHITECTURE.md` | Generated accepted architecture decisions |
| `.agents/AGENTS.md` | Generated active operating rules (also root `CONTRIBUTING.md`) |
| `.agents/README.md` | Generated public overview (also root `README.md`) |
| `.agents/PLAN.md` | Human-authored near-term plan and verification gates |
| `.agents/SCRATCHPAD.md` | Non-normative temporary notes |
| `.agents/notes/` | Published README sections and private working notes (`TODO.md` is not published) |
| `.agents/requests/` | Independently reviewable requirement records |
| `.agents/decisions/` | Independently reviewable architecture decisions |
| `.agents/rules/` | Independently reviewable mandatory rules |
| `.agents/agents/` | Portable agent role descriptions |
| `.agents/skills/` | Portable task procedures (`<name>/SKILL.md`) |
| `.github/` | GitHub CI, workflows and repo management scripts |
| `repo.dfconfig` | DarkFactory repository declaration and GitHub protection policy |
| `VERSION` | Canonical SemVer without a leading `v` |
| `LICENSE` | GPL-3.0 license text |

The source folders are independent. Edit source records, never their generated projections. Use Git links rather than copied root documentation.

_Source: [0002-layout.md](notes/0002-layout.md)_


## Contribution and delivery

Use `development` as the integration branch. Work in a focused topic branch and propose the change into `development`. After review and verification, publish `development` into `main` using a release pull request.

The repository bumps `VERSION` once per same-repository PR, checks generated documents, restricts `main` PR sources to `development`, and automatically tags/publishes releases on `main` pushes. These workflows are not substitutes for GitHub's **native** branch protection.

Useful command:

```bash
python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --write
python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py'
```

For task-specific guidance, select a role from `.agents/agents/` and skills from `.agents/skills/`. Treat them as portable instructions: a harness must explicitly load them to execute them.

_Source: [0003-contribution.md](notes/0003-contribution.md)_


## GitHub administration

The live `main` protection requirement is tracked separately from the repository declaration. A configuration file alone does not protect a GitHub branch. Using a GitHub CLI login that has repository administration privileges, apply and verify the policy:

```bash
python3 .github/scripts/apply_branch_protection.py
python3 .github/scripts/apply_branch_protection.py --apply
```

The script reads `repo.dfconfig` and refuses unapproved replacement of existing divergent protection. Until GitHub reports `main.protected = true`, do not claim enforcement is complete. Native review settings may require an eligible reviewer other than the PR author.

_Source: [0004-administration.md](notes/0004-administration.md)_
